newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish premier prays for politician killed by ETA.
newsitem.headline: Spanish premier prays for politician killed by ETA.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, surrounded by members of his government and hundreds of worshippers, prayed for peace at a mass on Wednesday for a politician killed by Basque separatist group ETA.

ETA earlier declared it would accept the "crude and painful" consequences of its killing of 29-year-old Basque town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco earlier this month. Blanco was a low-ranking member of Aznar's Popular Party. Archbishop of Madrid Antonio Maria Rouco, who led the memorial service at the cathedral adjoining the royal palace, said he hoped Blanco's killing would bear fruit and bring an end to violence.

"There is nothing more human and divine which we can desire...in this mass for Miguel Angel Blanco than the conversion of those who killed him and those who cultivate this atmosphere of hatred among young," Rouco said.
"If this happens, we will find ourselves with all certainty at the beginning of the end of terrorism in our homeland," he added.
Aznar, who has promised a crackdown on ETA and its supporters, did not speak at the mass but sang hymns and uttered prayers.

The archbishop said Blanco had been subjected to "unspeakable torture" adding: "This action was born in the darkest reaches of the human personality." He saw the social clamour following Blanco's death was a sign of hope.
Blanco's killing touched off an unprecedented outcry of condemnation in Spain. Millions of angry Spaniards demonstrated last week to demand an end to ETA violence.
In its first communique since the assassination, ETA formally claimed responsibility on Wednesday.
The group had left no doubt of its involvement.

It kidnapped Blanco on July 10 and gave the government a 48-hour deadline to transfer 500 ETA inmates scattered around the country to Basque prisons. Two days later, the guerrillas shot Blanco twice in the head and dumped him on a roadside.

"ETA assumes and will assume in the future, with its head held high, the consequences of the conflict as crude and painful as they may be," the group said in a statement published in the radical Basque newspaper Egin, its usual mouthpiece.

"ETA assumes, through this communique, total responsibility for the arrest, and later execution after the 48-hour deadline passed, of the Popular Party member and Ermua town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco," it said.

ETA, which has killed around 800 people in a violent campaign for a Basque state over the past 29 years, reiterated that it was ready to lay down its arms if the government met its demands for Basque self-determination.
"The Spanish government knows for sure that ETA's hand is held out for peace," the group said. The government has refused to negotiate with ETA until it renounces violence.
